```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Das_2019_ceftaroline")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dky439> (open access, PMC6337900)
* Supplementary data (Supplementary Methods = covariate-model forms;
  Table S2 = demographics; Table S3 = final parameter estimates; Tables S4-S7 =
  probability of target attainment, PTA): supplementary data of the same DOI.

Ceftaroline fosamil is an N-phosphono prodrug that plasma phosphatases convert
rapidly to ceftaroline, an anti-MRSA cephalosporin. Das 2019 pooled 21 clinical
studies (951 subjects) into a joint population PK model of the prodrug and the
active moiety and used it to simulate PTA in patients with complicated skin and
soft tissue infection (cSSTI) for ceftaroline fosamil 600 mg q12h by 1 h
infusion and 600 mg q8h by 2 h infusion, with renal dose adjustment. Those
simulations supported the European approval of the q8h regimen for
*Staphylococcus aureus* with ceftaroline MICs of 2 or 4 mg/L and the EUCAST q8h
breakpoints.

The model belongs to the same development lineage as
`Riccobene_2016_ceftaroline` and `Riccobene_2017_ceftaroline` (same sponsor,
overlapping authors, same covariate set) but was re-estimated on a larger pooled
dataset, so its parameter values differ from both.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- readModelDb("Das_2019_ceftaroline")()$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "n_studies", "age_range", "weight_range",
          "sex_female_pct", "race_ethnicity")])
```

The dataset (Supplementary Table S2) held 2575 ceftaroline fosamil and 8174
ceftaroline concentrations from 951 subjects: 501 male and 450 female, median
age 50 years (12-93), median weight 73 kg (40-134), median BSA-normalised
creatinine clearance 95.8 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (6.7-467.4). 267 (28%) were healthy
volunteers and 684 (72%) patients (463 cSSTI, 214 community-acquired pneumonia,
7 suspected infection). All studies dosed intravenously except one intramuscular
phase 1 study.

# Virtual cohort

The article simulated 5000 cSSTI patients per scenario, resampling the baseline
covariates of the cSSTI patients in the modelling dataset for normal renal
function and drawing covariates within each renal-function band otherwise, with
creatinine clearance uniform within the band. Those individual covariates are
not published, so this cohort is a stand-in (see Assumptions): 200 patients per
arm, weight log-normal around 78 kg truncated to the dataset range 40-134 kg,
age normal around 45 years (normal renal function) or 60 years (renal
impairment) truncated to 18-93 years. Normal renal function draws creatinine
clearance above 80 mL/min/1.73 m^2; because the renal term saturates at 80, the
exact distribution above 80 does not enter clearance. Truncation is by
reject-and-redraw, never by clamping.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190211)
set.seed(20190211)

draw_trunc <- function(n, gen, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- gen(n)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

n_per_arm <- 200

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,           ~renal,     ~dose_mg, ~tau_h, ~dur_h, ~crcl_lo, ~crcl_hi, ~esrd,
  "q12h normal",   "normal",   600,      12,     1,      80,       200,      0,
  "q8h normal",    "normal",   600,       8,     2,      80,       200,      0,
  "q12h mild",     "mild",     600,      12,     1,      50,        80,      0,
  "q12h moderate", "moderate", 400,      12,     1,      30,        50,      0,
  "q12h severe",   "severe",   300,      12,     1,      15,        30,      0,
  "q12h ESRD",     "ESRD",     200,      12,     1,       5,        15,      1,
  "q8h mild",      "mild",     600,       8,     2,      50,        80,      0,
  "q8h moderate",  "moderate", 400,       8,     2,      30,        50,      0,
  "q8h severe",    "severe",   300,       8,     2,      15,        30,      0,
  "q8h ESRD",      "ESRD",     200,       8,     2,       5,        15,      1
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm))

cohort <- arms |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    arm = arm, renal = renal, dose_mg = dose_mg, tau_h = tau_h, dur_h = dur_h,
    WT = draw_trunc(n_per_arm, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(78), 0.22), 40, 134),
    AGE = draw_trunc(n_per_arm,
                     function(k) rnorm(k, if (renal == "normal") 45 else 60, 15),
                     18, 93),
    CRCL = if (renal == "normal") {
      draw_trunc(n_per_arm, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(115), 0.3), 80, 300)
    } else {
      runif(n_per_arm, crcl_lo, crcl_hi)
    },
    RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = esrd
  ) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), DIS_HEALTHY = 0, RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 0)

cohort |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(n = n(), WT = median(WT), AGE = median(AGE), CRCL = median(CRCL),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(c(WT, AGE, CRCL), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "N" = n, "Median weight (kg)" = WT,
                "Median age (y)" = AGE,
                "Median CrCL (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = CRCL) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Simulation

Steady state is imposed with `ss = 1` on the first dose and one dosing interval
is observed on a 0.05 h grid. Residual error is not used (the article fixed it
to zero for PTA); `Cc_ceftaroline` is the individual prediction.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Das_2019_ceftaroline")

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg, dur = dur_h, evid = 1L, ii = tau_h, ss = 1L,
         cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)

obs_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(rel = seq(0, 1, length.out = 241)) |>
  mutate(time = rel * tau_h, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0L, ii = 0,
         ss = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 2L) |>
  select(-rel)

events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

# One rxSolve call per arm keeps each call small. useLinCmt = FALSE keeps the
# two-endpoint dvid mapping intact. The steady-state solve is knife-edge on
# liblsoda, rxode2's default: perturbing the thetas by 1e-12 (relative) leaves
# one subject non-finite ("excess work done") in about one solve in four. The
# Fortran LSODA (`method = "lsoda"`) and cvode solve all of them.
sim <- lapply(levels(events$arm), function(a) {
  ev_a <- events[events$arm == a, , drop = FALSE]
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, events = ev_a,
    keep = c("arm", "renal", "dose_mg", "tau_h"),
    useLinCmt = FALSE, maxsteps = 1e6, method = "lsoda"
  ) |> as.data.frame()
}) |> bind_rows()

stopifnot(nrow(sim) == nrow(obs_rows), all(is.finite(sim$Cc_ceftaroline)))
```

## Structural identity: AUC over a steady-state interval is the formation rate over clearance

Ceftaroline fosamil is converted completely, mol for mol, so at steady state the
ceftaroline AUC over one dosing interval is
`dose * (604.7 / 684.7) / CLc`. Both sides use the same drawn parameters; the
only difference is trapezoidal error, so the bound is tight.

```{r identity}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

ident <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(auc_tau = trap(time, Cc_ceftaroline), cl = first(cl_ceftaroline),
            dose_mg = first(dose_mg), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(expected = dose_mg * (604.7 / 684.7) / cl,
         rel_err = auc_tau / expected - 1)

cat("max |relative error| of AUCtau,ss vs dose x MW ratio / CLc:",
    signif(max(abs(ident$rel_err)), 3), "\n")
stopifnot(max(abs(ident$rel_err)) < 0.01)
```

## Steady-state profiles

```{r fig-profiles, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc_ceftaroline),
            lo = quantile(Cc_ceftaroline, 0.05),
            hi = quantile(Cc_ceftaroline, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm, ncol = 5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
       y = "Total ceftaroline (mg/L)",
       title = "Simulated steady-state ceftaroline, median and 90% interval") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```

# PKNCA validation

The article reports no noncompartmental results, so PKNCA is used to summarise
the simulated steady-state exposures per arm and to confirm independently of
the trapezoid above that the interval AUC equals the formation rate over
clearance.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  select(id, arm, time, Cc_ceftaroline) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc_ceftaroline)) |>
  as.data.frame()
# The ss = 1 solve returns the steady-state trough at time 0.
stopifnot(all(table(conc_df$id[conc_df$time == 0]) == 1))

dose_df <- dose_rows |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt, dur) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc_ceftaroline ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, duration = "dur")

intervals <- arms |>
  select(arm, end = tau_h) |>
  mutate(start = 0, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE) |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tidy <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast"))

nca_tidy |>
  group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Cmax,ss (mg/L)" = cmax,
                "Cmin,ss (mg/L)" = cmin, "AUCtau,ss (mg*h/L)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable()

auc_chk <- nca_tidy |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, auclast = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(ident |> select(id, expected), by = "id")
stopifnot(nrow(auc_chk) == nrow(cohort),
          max(abs(auc_chk$auclast / auc_chk$expected - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Probability of target attainment

%fT>MIC is the percentage of the steady-state dosing interval during which the
free concentration (80% of total, Methods) exceeds the MIC. The PK/PD targets
for *S. aureus* are 27% (stasis), 31% (1-log10 kill) and 35% (2-log10 kill)
fT>MIC (Table 1).

```{r ftmic}
mics <- c(0.015, 0.03, 0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
fu <- 0.8

# Grid points in [0, tau): the last point (time = tau) repeats time 0.
ft <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(time < max(time)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  tidyr::crossing(mic = mics) |>
  group_by(arm, renal, id, mic) |>
  summarise(ftmic = 100 * mean(fu * Cc_ceftaroline > mic), .groups = "drop")

targets <- c(stasis = 27, kill1 = 31, kill2 = 35)
pta_sim <- ft |>
  tidyr::crossing(tibble(target_name = names(targets), target = targets)) |>
  group_by(arm, mic, target_name) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ftmic >= target), .groups = "drop")
```

## Tables 2 and 3 and Figures 1 and 2: normal renal function

```{r pub-tables-2-3}
# Das 2019 Table 2 (600 mg q12h 1 h) and Table 3 (600 mg q8h 2 h), PTA (%) by
# MIC for 27 / 31 / 35 % fT>MIC; MIC 0.015-1 are 100 in every column.
pub23 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,          ~mic, ~stasis, ~kill1, ~kill2,
  "q12h normal",    2,    98.9,   96.1,   92.5,
  "q12h normal",    4,    66.5,   49.5,   37.1,
  "q12h normal",    8,    4.84,   2.14,   1.04,
  "q12h normal",   16,    0.04,      0,      0,
  "q8h normal",     2,     100,    100,    100,
  "q8h normal",     4,    98.7,   96.8,   93.6,
  "q8h normal",     8,    42.9,   33.1,   23.4,
  "q8h normal",    16,    0.72,   0.38,   0.22
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(stasis, kill1, kill2), names_to = "target_name",
               values_to = "pta_pub")

pta_norm <- pta_sim |>
  filter(arm %in% c("q12h normal", "q8h normal")) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm))

ggplot(pta_norm, aes(mic, pta, colour = target_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = pub23, aes(y = pta_pub), shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics, labels = format(mics, drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c(kill1 = "1-log kill (31%)",
                                   kill2 = "2-log kill (35%)",
                                   stasis = "stasis (27%)")) +
  labs(x = "Ceftaroline MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = "Target",
       title = "PTA by MIC, normal renal function",
       caption = "Lines: simulation. Crosses: Das 2019 Tables 2 and 3 (replicates Figures 1 and 2 without the AWARE MIC histograms).") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

pta_norm |>
  inner_join(pub23, by = c("arm", "mic", "target_name")) |>
  mutate(pta = round(pta, 1)) |>
  arrange(arm, mic, target_name) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic, "Target" = target_name,
                "Simulated PTA (%)" = pta, "Published PTA (%)" = pta_pub) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Gate: the median fT>MIC across the MIC range (Tables S4 and S5)

A PTA at a single target collapses towards 0 or 100% and moves steeply with
exposure, so it is a poor assertion. Tables S4 and S5 print PTA for targets
from 20% to 100% fT>MIC, which traces the whole distribution of fT>MIC at each
MIC; the target at which PTA crosses 50% is the published *median* fT>MIC. The
simulated median is compared with it at every MIC where it is not censored at
100%.

```{r gate-median}
# Supplementary Table S4 (q12h 1 h) and S5 (q8h 2 h): PTA (%) at fT>MIC targets
# 20, 30, ..., 100 %.
s4s5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,          ~mic,  ~t20,  ~t30,  ~t40,  ~t50,  ~t60,  ~t70,  ~t80,  ~t90, ~t100,
  "q12h normal",  0.5,   100,   100,   100, 99.76,  97.1, 89.44, 74.42, 54.46,  34.5,
  "q12h normal",    1,   100,   100, 99.28, 93.78, 78.74,  55.2, 32.14, 16.46,  7.82,
  "q12h normal",    2,   100, 97.48, 83.14, 55.58, 28.32, 11.54,  4.24,  1.38,  0.42,
  "q12h normal",    4,  92.2, 55.86, 22.16,  6.52,  1.54,  0.36,  0.12,  0.06,  0.02,
  "q8h normal",     2,   100,   100,  99.9, 98.58, 93.48, 81.54, 64.34, 46.08, 29.92,
  "q8h normal",     4, 99.82, 97.56, 85.86, 63.32, 41.14,  23.2, 11.74,  5.74,  2.32,
  "q8h normal",     8, 64.86, 36.48,  14.6,  5.76,     2,  0.66,  0.14,  0.08,  0.02
)

# Linear interpolation of the 50% crossing of PTA (decreasing in target).
median_from_pta <- function(pta) {
  tg <- c(0, seq(20, 100, by = 10))
  # approx() needs increasing x; the repeated 100s sit far from the 50% crossing.
  approx(rev(c(100, pta)), rev(tg), xout = 50, ties = mean)$y
}
pub_med <- s4s5 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(med_pub = median_from_pta(c_across(t20:t100))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(arm, mic, med_pub)

sim_med <- ft |>
  filter(arm %in% c("q12h normal", "q8h normal")) |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  group_by(arm, mic) |>
  summarise(med_sim = median(ftmic), .groups = "drop")

med_cmp <- pub_med |>
  left_join(sim_med, by = c("arm", "mic")) |>
  mutate(diff = med_sim - med_pub)

med_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(med_pub, med_sim, diff), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
                "Published median fT>MIC (%)" = med_pub,
                "Simulated median fT>MIC (%)" = med_sim,
                "Difference (points)" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  nrow(med_cmp) == 7, !anyNA(med_cmp$med_sim),
  # Centre: an unrestricted renal term shifts every row down by about 13
  # points on average.
  abs(mean(med_cmp$diff)) < 3,
  # Envelope, wide enough for 200-subject sampling noise in a median.
  max(abs(med_cmp$diff)) < 7
)
```

## Sensitivity: two readings the article leaves open

Two parts of the covariate model are not fully pinned by the printed table (see
Assumptions): whether the renal term is restricted to values below 80
mL/min/1.73 m^2, and whether the printed CLc and Vcc are the healthy-volunteer
or the patient values. Each alternative is re-simulated for the two
normal-renal-function arms with the same subjects and compared with the same
published medians.

```{r sensitivity}
med_for <- function(m) {
  ev <- events[events$arm %in% c("q12h normal", "q8h normal"), , drop = FALSE]
  ev$arm <- droplevels(ev$arm)
  s <- lapply(levels(ev$arm), function(a) {
    rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190211)
    rxode2::rxSolve(m, events = ev[ev$arm == a, , drop = FALSE], keep = "arm",
                    useLinCmt = FALSE, maxsteps = 1e6, method = "lsoda") |>
      as.data.frame()
  }) |> bind_rows()
  s |>
    group_by(id) |>
    filter(time < max(time)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    tidyr::crossing(mic = unique(pub_med$mic)) |>
    group_by(arm, id, mic) |>
    summarise(ftmic = 100 * mean(fu * Cc_ceftaroline > mic), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(arm, mic) |>
    summarise(med_sim = median(ftmic), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
    inner_join(pub_med, by = c("arm", "mic")) |>
    mutate(diff = med_sim - med_pub)
}

variants <- list(
  "As packaged (renal term below 80; printed values are healthy)" = mod,
  "Renal term unrestricted above 80" = mod |>
    rxode2::model(crcl_cl <- (CRCL / ref_crcl)^(e_crcl_cl_ceftaroline * (1 - RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS))),
  "Printed CLc and Vcc are the patient values" = mod |>
    rxode2::ini(e_dis_healthy_cl_ceftaroline = 1, e_dis_healthy_vc_ceftaroline = 1)
)
sens <- lapply(names(variants), function(v) med_for(variants[[v]]) |> mutate(variant = v)) |>
  bind_rows()

sens_summary <- sens |>
  group_by(variant) |>
  summarise(mean_diff = mean(diff), max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff)), .groups = "drop")

sens_summary |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Variant" = variant, "Mean difference (points)" = mean_diff,
                "Largest absolute difference (points)" = max_abs_diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

sens |>
  select(variant, arm, mic, diff) |>
  mutate(diff = round(diff, 1)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variant, values_from = diff) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated minus published median fT>MIC (points)")

# The unrestricted renal term is excluded by the published PTA: it moves the
# whole distribution down by many points.
unres <- sens_summary$mean_diff[sens_summary$variant == "Renal term unrestricted above 80"]
stopifnot(unres < -6)
```

The unrestricted renal term misses every published median in the same
direction, so the restriction below 80 is retained. The two orientations of the
patient multipliers, in contrast, both land within a few points of the
published medians: a higher clearance and a larger central volume in patients
act in opposite directions on fT>MIC and largely cancel. The packaged
orientation fits somewhat closer, but the margin is small next to the
uncertainty of the stand-in covariate cohort, so the PTA tables do not settle
the orientation; it is taken from the wording of the table (see Assumptions).

## Tables S6 and S7: renal impairment with dose adjustment

```{r pub-s6-s7}
# Supplementary Tables S6 (q12h 1 h) and S7 (q8h 2 h); MIC <= 1 (q12h) and
# <= 2 (q8h) are ~100 in every column and are omitted.
pub67 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,            ~mic, ~stasis, ~kill1, ~kill2,
  "q12h mild",        4,   81.62,  69.24,  58.10,
  "q12h mild",        8,   12.24,   6.86,   4.20,
  "q12h moderate",    4,   72.10,  59.50,  49.50,
  "q12h moderate",    8,    5.76,   3.24,   1.98,
  "q12h severe",      4,   72.74,  63.70,  56.34,
  "q12h severe",      8,    5.68,   3.84,   2.68,
  "q12h ESRD",        4,   69.74,  63.28,  58.24,
  "q12h ESRD",        8,    5.58,   4.42,   3.60,
  "q8h mild",         4,   99.62,  99.02,  97.44,
  "q8h mild",         8,   59.04,  49.28,  40.14,
  "q8h moderate",     4,   98.10,  96.46,  94.14,
  "q8h moderate",     8,   35.62,  29.34,  23.62,
  "q8h severe",       4,   97.28,  95.88,  93.64,
  "q8h severe",       8,   34.38,  29.32,  25.32,
  "q8h ESRD",         4,   94.90,  93.68,  92.30,
  "q8h ESRD",         8,   30.10,  27.22,  24.50
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(stasis, kill1, kill2), names_to = "target_name",
               values_to = "pta_pub")

renal_cmp <- pta_sim |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm)) |>
  inner_join(pub67, by = c("arm", "mic", "target_name")) |>
  mutate(diff = pta - pta_pub)

renal_cmp |>
  filter(target_name == "stasis") |>
  mutate(across(c(pta, diff), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  select(arm, mic, pta, pta_pub, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
                "Simulated PTA, stasis (%)" = pta,
                "Published PTA, stasis (%)" = pta_pub,
                "Difference (points)" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

# The ESRD multiplier replaces the creatinine-clearance term. Applying both
# would cut ESRD clearance a further threefold ((10/80)^0.54 = 0.33) and lift
# PTA at MIC 8 far above the published 5.6% (q12h) and 30% (q8h).
esrd8 <- renal_cmp |> filter(grepl("ESRD", arm), mic == 8, target_name == "stasis")
stopifnot(nrow(esrd8) == 2, all(esrd8$pta < 60))
# Centre of all 48 renal-impairment cells.
stopifnot(abs(median(renal_cmp$diff)) < 8)
```

The renal-impairment cohorts are the least certain part of this replication:
the article drew their covariates from a multivariate distribution that is not
published, and PTA near MIC 4-8 sits on the steep part of the curve. The checks
above therefore assert only the centre of the differences and the structural
ESRD result.

# Assumptions and deviations

## Errata and departures from a literal reading of the source

* **Patient-status orientation.** Table S3 prints 'Patient status effect' on CLc
  (1.16) and Vcc (1.59), and the Supplementary Methods define a categorical
  effect as `theta_TV,REF * theta_x^X`, but the sentence defining `X` is garbled
  ("equal to 1 or 0 dependent on an individual being categorised into the
  reference group or not"). The model takes the printed CLc and Vcc as the
  healthy-volunteer values and applies the multipliers to patients, because the
  rows are labelled as the effect of patient status, the preceding sentence of
  the Supplementary Methods applies `theta_x` to "the group different from the
  reference group", and the sibling model `Riccobene_2017_ceftaroline` uses the
  same orientation. The published PTA does not clearly discriminate between the
  two orientations (Sensitivity section): both land within a few points of the
  median fT>MIC of Tables S4 and S5, the packaged one somewhat closer. The
  orientation matters for simulations of healthy
  volunteers, whose clearance and central volume are 1.16- and 1.59-fold lower
  than patients' under this reading and 1.16- and 1.59-fold higher under the
  other.
* **Renal term saturates at 80 mL/min/1.73 m^2.** Table S3 prints the term as
  `(NCrCL/80)^0.54` with no restriction. Both sibling models of this lineage
  (`Riccobene_2016_ceftaroline`, `Riccobene_2017_ceftaroline`) restrict it to
  values below 80, and the article's normal-renal-function PTA confirms it: the
  unrestricted form gives higher clearance in subjects above 80 and
  under-predicts every published median fT>MIC (Sensitivity section).
* **ESRD replaces the renal term.** The ESRD multiplier (0.34) is applied in
  place of the creatinine-clearance term, as in the sibling models; applying
  both contradicts the ESRD rows of Tables S6 and S7 (see the check above).
* **Hemodialysis-session clearance.** 'CLc, dialysis' = 11.18 is printed without
  a unit or an equation. It is encoded, as in `Riccobene_2017_ceftaroline`, as
  the ceftaroline clearance (L/h) that replaces the body clearance while a
  session runs (`RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 1`). No simulation in the article
  involves a dialysis session, so this term is not validated here.
* **Intramuscular absorption.** The Results text calls the intramuscular input a
  "zero-order absorption component", but Table S3 prints Kacf = 0.53 with unit
  h^-1 (a first-order rate constant) and IIV on it. The table is followed:
  first-order absorption from `depot`. Intramuscular bioavailability is not
  printed and is taken as 1 (the sibling models fix it to 1). The intravenous
  regimens validated here do not use the depot.
* **Allometric scaling of Q and Vp.** The article says body weight was applied
  allometrically to "CL and V of both ceftaroline and ceftaroline fosamil" with
  exponents 0.75 and 1 at 70 kg. It is applied to every clearance (including
  intercompartmental) and every volume, as in the sibling models.
* **Variance scale.** Table S3 prints IIV as CVs. They are carried as
  `omega^2 = CV^2`, the convention of the sibling models from the same sponsor,
  where the printed CV equals the square root of the variance. For ceftaroline
  the alternative `log(CV^2 + 1)` differs by less than 4%; it differs more for
  the two prodrug etas (0.846 vs 0.624), which do not affect ceftaroline exposure
  because the prodrug is converted completely within minutes.
* **Residual error on one random effect.** 'IIV Eta on Epsilon' (CV 0.6) is
  encoded as `etaRUV` scaling the additive and proportional SDs of both analytes.
* **Units.** The model was fitted in micromol/L with a molar 100% conversion.
  This implementation doses ceftaroline fosamil in mg and reports both analytes
  in mg/L: the conversion flux is scaled by the molar-mass ratio 604.7/684.7
  (ceftaroline / ceftaroline fosamil, g/mol; the same constants as
  `Chauzy_2022_ceftaroline`), and the printed additive SDs are converted to mg/L
  (0.12 umol/L x 0.6847 = 0.0822 mg/L; 0.063 umol/L x 0.6047 = 0.0381 mg/L).
  Molar masses are not printed in the article.
* **Age effect.** Applied to every subject as `(AGE/36)^-0.23`, the printed form
  (also the form of `Riccobene_2016_ceftaroline`); the reference 36 years is not
  the dataset median of 50 despite the Supplementary Methods saying reference
  values are medians.

## Simulation assumptions

* The cSSTI patient covariates resampled by the article are not published. The
  stand-in cohort (weight median 78 kg, age median 45 years for normal renal
  function and 60 years for renal impairment) is an assumption; ceftaroline
  clearance depends on age only weakly (exponent -0.23), and above 80
  mL/min/1.73 m^2 not at all on creatinine clearance, so the normal-renal-
  function comparison depends mainly on weight.
* Creatinine clearance in mL/min (the article's renal bands) is used as the
  BSA-normalised value.
* ESRD subjects are flagged `RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = 1` with no dialysis session
  in the simulated interval.
* 200 simulated patients per arm, against 5000 in the article.
* The solves use the Fortran LSODA (`method = "lsoda"`). The default liblsoda
  fails the steady-state solve of an occasional subject after a last-bit change
  in the parameters (see the Simulation section).
